page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 67,610.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,690.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4,103.87 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 277.75 GB/sec. Single-core performance remains in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,777.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,689.08.

The CPU architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. This is reflected in strong benchmark results for specialized tasks, including software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 41,502.0 and LLM prompt processing, where it processed 229.23 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Database operations are highly efficient, demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 30,504.05 and Redis SET throughput of 70.46 million operations per second. These characteristics make the instance highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is an x86_64 general-purpose server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 256 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel processor with 260 MB of L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. While single-core performance is average, the instance delivers strong multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities, with uncached read speeds of 277.75 GB/sec. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight its efficiency in database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference, processing 229.23 tokens/sec on a 7B model. This profile makes it highly suitable for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, database hosting, and static web serving.
